properties.content:
Report Details

Violation ID: 861412
Permit API: 033-26975
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Lawrence Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-09-06
Comments: Routine site inspection at Seneca Resources SGL 90 well pad on September 6, 2019. Wells 033-26976 and 033-26977 have been plugged. Both plugged wells have been backfilled. Well 033-26975 remains in regulatory inactive status. Well cellar is full of water with a conductivity reading of 124 uS/cm. This well has three annular vents extending above ground level, tied together, open, and lined out to a container through a rubber hose. The poly container is stationed on secondary containment. Two small spills were observed during my site inspection. Spill one is adjacent to the poly container and is ~ 4'L x 2'W. Spill two is near the well cellar and is ~ 2'L x 2'W (see attached photos). Neither spill left the site. While onsite I left a voice message for Seneca Resources EHS representative Jeff Passerrello. Mr. Passerrello returned my call at ~1445 and stated he will be sending a crew for clean ups and notify me once its completed. Mr. Passerrello sent me an email on 9/8/19 with pictures stated that the clean-up was completed on the evening of 9/6/19. Violations were cited and immediately corrected.

Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
Violation ID: 940199
Permit API: 115-20058
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Auburn Twp

Inspection Date: 12/16/2021
Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72hr. Pressure Build Up Tests (PBUTs) being performed on the (2) wells on the Blanche-Poulsen pad, they are the 1H and the 2H. These PBUTs are being performed as part of an ongoing gas migration investigation underway in the area. - Review of CALLC's recently drilled Koromlan 107HC Area of Review "AOR" map shows the close proximity of this new wells lateral to these existing wells. (See attached Koromlan 107HC AOR map.) - Upon arrival the (8 5/8"x5 1/2") annuli of both wells, the (11 3/4"x 8 5/8") of the 2H and the 1H (16"x 8 5/8") w/ the (11 3/4") annulus covered by a single cap were shut in for testing. - At the 1H, the (16x11 3/4") and the(11 3/4"x8 5/8") annuli are capped with (1) cap due to 11 3/4" casing being below the 16" and 8 5/8" casing. The 2H (16"x11 3/4") annulus is covered by cement. - Both cellars are back filled to ground level w/ large gravels. - There was no active bubbling noted in the ponded water around the 1H. The 2H had no water at ground level. I met with CALLC Field Rep. Craig Shores and Creston Consultant Reps., Kevin Leaman and Andrew Pfisterer. Starting at approx. 07:15 ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. - Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below: - 1H (16x11) annulus: Not sure which annulus has gas due to single cap covering the (16x11 and 11x8) annuli. **see (11x8) annulus for results** (11x8) annulus: 2 psi.; 100% gas, Sample taken @ 07:30 ** Pressure in the (16x8) shared vent appears to be a new occurrence since last PBUT on 11/18/2021.** (8x5) annulus: 0 psi.; 50% gas, Sample taken @ 07:35 - 2H (16x11): annulus is cemented over (11x8) annulus: 25 psi.; 100% gas, Sample taken @ 07:50 (8x5) annulus: 0 psi.; 25,420 ppm dropping to 0% gas, No sample taken - Both wells annuli were returned to open and venting to temporary poly tanks @ 08:10. ** Due to the probable impact of these wells defective conditions on the on going gas migration in the area, if not corrected, additional violations may be issued.

The water appears to be exiting the level spreader in sheet flow, but appears to be channelizing as it exits the LOD into the tree line. Violation ID: 855653
Permit API: 081-20566
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-07-15
Comments: On July 15, 2019, Department representative Brad Kline and Jared Jacobini conducted an investigation of production fluid leak at the Range Resources Bobst Mountain 18-23H Pad. The Department met with Kirby Steck with Range Resources, he stated that upon excavation of the dump line of the GPU, they did not find a rock guard around the line. Range Resources is suspecting that this caused the hole in the dump line. Range Resources estimated about 1.25 barrel of production fluid had leaked out of the line. At the time of inspection, Range Resources had excavated down to the dump line but were waiting on another piece of equipment to continue removing the impacted soil. A 10'x15' area of impact had been excavated but more soil beneath the dump line needs to be removed. The impacted soil is being placed into covered 25 yard roll back dumpsters. At the time about 2.5 dumpsters had been filled. The release of production fluid caused by the hole in the dump line is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), 78a.54, and Section 301 of the Solid Waste Management Act. Due to the volume of production fluid leaked, remediation under Act 2 is required under 78a.66(c).

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/07/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions Pad B after the a notification from the operator that additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC) was discovered once rig mats were removed from the dancefloor on the pad. The operator stated in their notification that they believed that this fluid could be associated with the reported produced fluid release from 2/3/23. Two snubbing units are in operation on Pad B. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on the pad. He first showed me the area where rig mats and timber mats had been removed from a portion of the dancefloor. He stated that they couldn't remove any more of the rig mats and timber mats until the snubbing units finished the drill out because the flare stack was sitting on the dancefloor. The fluid present in the area of the removed rig mats had an EC between 3.45 mS/cm toward the southern end and >19.99 mS/cm at the northern end. Mr. Subra said that the clam shell boxes had been placed on this area of the dancefloor which they believed had released elevated EC fluid to this area of the pad. He stated that it is against EQT policy to stage the boxes on the well pad without secondary containment but that a contractor had done so anyway.A crew was excavating this area during this inspection. The roll-off box that they were placing the excavated material in was sitting on the rig mats to the west of the uncovered area but did not have any kind of secondary containment underneath it. The Department recommends adding secondary containment at least underneath the end of the roll-off box that has the door on it. In inspection report number 3492854, the Department noted the presence of a roll-box present on the dancefloor without secondary containment and the Department made the recommendation to place the box onto secondary containment.Next, Mr. Subra and I looked at the area on the east side of Pad B where fluid with elevated EC was found the day prior on 2/6/23. A crew was excavating this area as well during this inspection. The crew was placing the impacted pad material into an unlined roll-off box with a door on one end of the box. There was no secondary containment underneath any portion of the box and the box was visibly leaking fluid from the bottom of the door. I showed this to Mr. Subra and he stated that he thought it was melting ice. I recommended that the box be placed onto secondary containment regardless. He then stated that secondary containment could not be constructed for the box due to logistical constraints. I recommended that at a minimum a duckpond or tray of some sort be placed underneath door of the box. The EC of the fluid present in the area where sample 0718-203 was taken the day before was 15.95 mS/cm.I returned to the northwest area of the well pad and took sample 0718-204 from the fluid present where the rig mats and timber mats from the dancefloor had been removed. The sample was sent to the state laboratory the next day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al.Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release to Pad B from the clam shell boxes.

Report Details

Violation ID: 880968

Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Gibson Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-03-18
Comments: Brody Webster, contacted Gene Rickard by phone on March 17, 2020 at 4:27 PM to report that a spill had occurred on COG's Davis G Well Pad located in Gibson Township, Susquehanna County. The spill had occurred on March 14, 2020 at 10:00 AM while a service rig (Consolidated Wellsite Services) was on location to remove the 2 3/8-inch production tubing from the 2H well. During the operation, it was determined that there was debris (sand, shale fragments, etc.) within the production tubing causing fluid (primarily freshwater that had been introduced to the well) to be retained inside the pipe as it was brought to the surface. As each 30' segment of tubing was recovered and separated at the threaded connection, the fluid was drained from the pipe to the sealed well cellar (6' diameter metal cellar with cement base) and subsequently recovered by vacuum truck. During the process, a limited volume of the fluid sprayed/misted outside of the cellar and impacted an area of soil near the 2H well cellar. Approximately 7 to 8 cubic yards of visibly impacted soils were excavated and placed into a lined roll-off container for off-site disposal at an approved facility. Resource Environmental has been contracted to characterize the remaining soils. The reason the 2 3/8-inch pipes held water was because it was discovered that the pipe was plugged at the bottom by sand and other debris. Probably the reason for the pipes removal in the first place. The spill volume was reported as 22 gallons of produced and freshwater mixed together.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/14/2025
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8241009
Permit API: 015-23892
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/14/2025
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) on 7/14/2025 at 0630 hours. The weather ranged from mid-70s to mid-80s degrees throughout the day. The inspection was conducted in response to a report of a well control incident occurring on the 7H well which resulted in a release of produced fluids. Complaints Tracking System (CTS) ID #390569 is tied to the release in CTS.According to Repsol, at ~1830 hours on 7/13/2025 a pressure issue on the 7H well caused the uncontrolled release of produced fluid up the casing[s] to the pad surface. Efforts to control pressure and prevent the escaping fluids have failed so far. Secondary containments were overtopped and fluid has and continues to escape the pad surface. A temporary berm was constructed along the northwestern edge around the western corner of the pad, below the fill slope, to collect fluids (photos #3 to 5). The "corner" berm below the fill slope was said to be completed around 0000 hours on 7/14/2025. Numerous gravel berms were constructed on the pad surface to help prevent fluids from escaping the pad surface but are failing in numerous spots. Fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were observed sheet flowing from numerous areas along the southwestern edge of the pad (see photo #8 for example). Fluid observed in the western corner of the stormwater control basin was field measured for electrical conductivity and returned a reading of >19.99mS/cm. ~1000 hours: A Repsol representative onsite indicated that larger pumps were en route to catch up on fluid collection that is being pooled on the western corner of the well pad (photo #9). According to Repsol, the pumps being brought in should be able to catch up on the fluid that is pooled on the surface.A secondary berm/trench was constructed below the first "corner" berm below the fill slope sometime throughout the day. A break in the first berm was dug to allow fluid collected to flow into the secondary berm. The secondary berm is flowing fluid into the stormwater control basin onsite (see photos #10-12).Fluid was able to reach the stormwater control basin shown in photo #7. The DEP collected a sample for standard analysis code 942 from the basin which was field measured at >19.99mS/cm (Sample #0983-510).A third (tertiary) berm/trench was later constructed below the secondary berm and was built into the stormwater control basin. The short side wall of the basin was removed to allow for excess fluid build-up in the basin to collect in the third berm. The secondary and tertiary berms are utilized to relieve hydrostatic pressure from the "corner" berm. Fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were observed on the pad surface, in the constructed berms, in the pad's stormwater channels and in the stormwater control basin. Soils field measured at >4.00mS/cm were observed directly down-gradient of the well pad, below the constructed "corner" berm and along the installed surface waterline. Soils field measured at >4.00mS/cm were also observed along the surface waterline in the field adjacent to the pad (photo #13).Repsol identified and initiated the screening and sampling of nearby water supplies as required by 25 Pa. Code 78a.66b(4).Based on the findings of this inspection report, violations of the following are cited against API #015-23892 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, SWMA 301 and Clean Streams Law 401. A violation of 25 Pa. Code 78a.55(f) is cited against API #015-23892 as immediately corrected.I departed the well pad at 1430 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/02/2020
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 901085
Permit API: 081-21338
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lewis Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/02/2020
Comments: On December 2, 2020, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at Seneca Resources Gamble Pad K. No E&S issues were observed during the time of inspection. The site is stable and well vegetated meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. There are a total of 10 wells capable of producing located on this well pad. All wells are tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. There are 8 GPUs, 2 line heaters, and 3 steel vertical production fluids tanks onsite. Both GPUs, line heaters, and production fluid tanks were stationed in secondary containment. The DEP observed a Seneca Resources contractor pumping water from a well cellar and actively discharging the water off the the pad edge. The contractor provided the log sheet from today's field tests of pH and conductivity of the well cellar. The contractor stated that one well cellar is recorded on the log sheet due to the contractor logging only the highest conductivity of the 10 well cellars tested. The contractor stated that they had pumped out 7 of the well cellars prior to DEP arrival. The well cellar water was being discharged off the North pad edge. Well cellar water that was discharged had only travelled about 15 ft. downslope off the pad edge. There was no estimate of the amount of water pumped out of the 7 other well cellars prior to the DEP arrival.The discharge of water from a well cellar off the well pad is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 91.34(a).

Comments: On 1/11/23 a follow-up inspection of the Cartier/Luxner 4 OG Well site was conducted related to violations issued on 10/24/22 (IR: 3445085) and outstanding violations issued on 11/23/22 (IR: 3462090).Background:On 10/24/22, during a routine inspection, violations were issued for a brine release at the Cartier/Luxner 4 OG Well Site (IR: 3445085). Elevated conductivity was observed inside the earthen containment berm that surrounds the production tank. An operator response was received by the Department on 11/8/22 stating that the impacted material was removed and disposed of, and a new tank had been installed. On 11/23/22 a follow-up inspection was conducted and elevated conductivity was still observed in soil inside of the containment berm for the production tank (IR: 3462090). Outstanding violations were issued.Findings:-The area that exhibited elevated conductivity due to a leak in the corroded tank appeared to have been remediated. No elevated conductivity readings were obtained in that area of the containment (Photo #1). -The new tank was not hooked up to the well. -The pipe that had previously been attached to the old tank was not capped off (Photo #2), and a slow drip of fluid was observed coming from the pipe and hitting the ground below.-The substrate that was below the leaking pipe was stained and exhibited elevated conductivity (Photos #3-4).I informed Bryan Goletz of Diversified of my findings. According to Diversified in the NOV response dated 11/8/22 related to the first violations issued on 10/24/22, "The tank was not in service at the time of the inspection and the well doesn't produce fluid when in production". However, the fluid in the old tank during the initial inspection was at least shoulder height. And fluid is slowly, yet actively dripping from the pipe that should terminate at the tank. Outstanding violations of 78.57(a) and 78.54 are being issued.

Comments: On May 21, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Apollo's Dewitt 1 well located in Georges Township, Fayette County in response to IR 3924375 where violations were issued for failure to stabilize the access road. IR 3928781 documents the Operator response the Department received from Apollo Resource's representative James Stiffler on 2/2/2025, which stated that the hose the Department observed on the ground is equipment that is used for production, that they will grade the access road, and that they will confirm the well tag. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed what appears to be third-party disturbance along the beginning half of the access road. Grading and brush removal is observed until the road splits off in two direction, one of which leading directly to the Dewitt Well site. This portion of the road that leads to the well site is not graded and is still exhibiting signs of destabilization. The ruts previously observed during IR 3924375 appear to be deeper and filled with stormwater. The Department is requesting the Operator report any third party disturbance to the Department. At the time of this inspection, the well site was exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. Some minor rutting was also observed within the well site from what appears to be tire tracks. The Department is again recommending the Operator conduct maintenance on the access road to stabilize it and prevent any further erosion and sedimentation issues from occurring.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the wellhead that has incorrect Operator information posted on it, the Department is again recommending the Operator update the well tag to have accurate information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the wellhead.A meter box was and production tank was observed on site, the meter box had a well posting on it with the Operators information on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from the production tank or meter box. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for failure to stabilized the access road shall remain outstanding at this time.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT CHAP LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/13/2022
Violation Code: OGA3211(A) - WELL PERMITS - PERMIT REQUIRED - Drilling or altering a well without a well permit or no copy of the well permit at the well site.
Violation ID: 972772
Permit API: 129-29003
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Sewickley Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/13/2022
Comments: On October 13, 2022, the Department conducted a Routine inspection at the Sinay well pad in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself, ET Marcella Dantzler, those listed from the SWDO OG Team, and EQT representatives Joe Eversman and Logan Dominick.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the entrance of the access road, and was not obstructed by vegetation (see photo 2). The ER and PPC plans were not available immediately upon arrival (see photo 3). A site safety and environmental plan was found in the office onsite. A PPC plan was also in the office, but missing required components. Neither the secondary containment inspection records nor the well permit were available onsite when requested. A sediment basin was observed along the left side of the access road, looking towards the pad. A forebay cleanout was observed on the opposite side, with a culvert connecting them under the access road (see photo 5). Cattails were observed in the sediment basin. A further review will be conducted to ensure that they are part of the PCSM plan. A soil stockpile was observed along the left side of the access road, immediately before entering the pad (see photo 6). The operator was actively drilling onsite. This is the first well being drilled. The operator intends to drill 4 wells total. A destabilized area of soil was discovered behind the sound wall on the eastern side of the well pad (see photo 15). Preexisting metal and brick was observed outside of the LOD at this location, as was noted in the site E and S plans (see photo 16). A tear in the rig site containment was observed at the southern side of the pad. This was brought to Mr. Eversman's attention, who immediately called in a crew to repair it (see photo 12). Tanks and containers onsite that contained regulated substances were labelled, showed no evidence of leaks/discharges (see photos 13 and 14). The production tanks were within secondary containment (see photo 17). A puddle was observed at the northeastern corner of the containment. A soil conductivity reading was taken in this puddle, which read 200 Micro Siemens. The rig site containment appeared to be nearly full at its northeastern corner. A soil conductivity reading was taken at this corner, which read 390 Micro Siemens. The Department inquired with Mr. Eversman about whether the containment is pumped regularly. Mr. Eversman stated that the site containment gets pumped multiple times daily as needed. A pump truck later came to pump the containment during this inspection. A sediment-laden discharge to WOTC was discovered upon returning to the access road entrance (see photo 23). This discharge was flowing into a sewer drain that emptied into a field across the road from the well pad, through a culvert (see photo 21). This culvert was found to be approximately 80% full with sediment (see photo 22). Near the end of the inspection, EQT representative Logan Dominick arrived to the site, who was informed of the Department's findings. Mr. Dominick was able to provide an electronic copy of the PPC plan onsite, this was requested to be emailed to the Department for further review. He also stated to the Department that CFS and a silt pad will be installed around and over the sewer grate to prevent further discharge to the WOTC. He also stated that the site ERP and PPC plans had previously been placed into the mailboxes attached to the Act 9 sign, and that they were likely removed by a nuisance third party.Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that the aforementioned unstable soil spot behind the sound wall is re-stabilized. Violations are being issued for discharging to the waters of the commonwealth, failing to have an adequate ER AND PPC plan onsite, failing to have the drill permit onsite, and failing to have secondary containment inspection records onsite.

Violation ID: 8228894
Permit API: 125-29133
Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On April 9, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Schwotzer Arthur well site in Blaine Township, Washington County. An Erosion and Sediment (E and S) individual permit was issued by the Department for the site on January 26, 2024 and expires on January 25, 2029. This inspection was conducted in response to soil movement on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad and upslope of the northern corner of the well pad, which was reported to the Department by the operator on April 7, 2025. Range Resources representative Dennis Furmanek was present with the Department for this inspection. The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Stimulation operations are ongoing at the well pad at the time of this inspection (see photos 3 and 18). All containers onsite that appear to store regulated substances are placed within well pad secondary containment (see photo 20). All secondary containment onsite appears to be in good condition at the time of inspection with no holes or tears observed. The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 23). The GPU units onsite are equipped with secondary containment (see photo 24). Some areas of minor staining were observed on the surface of the well pad during this inspection. The E and S inspection log, E and S plan drawings, Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention, and Contingency (PPC) plan, E and S individual permit approval letter, secondary containment inspection, log, and well permits are onsite (see photos 19 and 25). Upon review onsite, the ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the information required by 78a.55.The access road appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 2). The soil crack that was reported by the operator on 4/07/2025 was present on the southwestern fill slope of well pad (see photos 4-9). It appears to be approximately 15 feet in length with saturated ground down slope of it, and no toe bulge observed below at the time of inspection. The Schwotzer to Hoskins pipeline is being constructed west of the well pad (see photo 11). The slough that was also reported by the operator on 4/07/2025 was present up slope of the northern corner of well pad (see photos 12-16). The operator estimates this area of soil movement to be approximately 25 feet wide by 30 feet long. This slough appears to pose the potential to threaten a stormwater channel down slope of it, if the displaced soil continues to move (see photo 17). Mr. Furmanek reported during this inspection that the operator intends to conduct repairs on these areas of soil movement once stimulation operations have been completed onsite and weather conditions allow for it. CFS that appears to be in need of maintenance was observed along the northeastern edge of the well pad (see photo 21).Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends the operator conduct general maintenance and housekeeping onsite to address the minor staining onsite and CFS maintenance needed. The Department also recommends that the operator monitor the soil crack on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad for any additional soil movement and implement temporary stabilization on the soil exposed by the slough north of the well pad.Violations shall be issued against the slough north of the well pad which could pose the potential to threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth. See NOV Response Comments.

Comments: On 02/21/2025 an Incident Response inspection was conducted at the DMC Well Site in response to an operator reported release.On 12/21/2024 Range Resources Representative, Derek Zofchak, reported an approximately 25 to 30-gallon release of reused water off containment at the DMC Well pad located in Donegal Township, Washington County.Range Resources representatives, Derek Zofchak and Denny Furmanek, were on site at the time of inspection. Mr. Furmanek and Mr. Zofchak informed the Department that that the release was discovered today (02/21/2025) at 10:55 am, that the quantity released was approximately 25 to 30 gallons, and that remediation efforts had already begun on the impacted area. The source of release was determined to be damaged secondary containment. The secondary containment had been damaged by a truck tire and the fluids on containment overtopped the containment berm and continued off an adjacent duck pond and onto the pad aggregate. Conductivity probe calibrated on 02/21/2025.The following was observed during the inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance. Various co-operations were taking place at the time of inspection and frac equipment was observed on site (Photos 1-2).-The area impacted by the release was observed. The area appeared to measure approximately 150 ft in length by 35 ft in width. Pooled fluid with a sheen was observed throughout the area. The damaged secondary containment was observed. It was made known that a crew was on site to repair the damaged containment. A vac truck was observed on site removing pooled fluids in the impacted area and on containment (Photos 3-5).-Field conductivity screening was conducted immediately in front of a large, gray electrical box. Over Range (greater than 20 ms/cm) field conductivity readings were observed (Photos 6-8).-Field conductivity screening was conducted throughout the impacted area. Elevated field screening values ranged between 7.21 ms/cm and greater than 20 ms/cm. The discharge onto the ground and failure to dispose of fluids, specifically produced fluid, are violations of 78a.54, 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act (SWMA) 301. The potential to have indirectly impacted Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) is a violation of 91.34(a) (Photos 9-12).-The extent of the impacts was observed where a non-elevated field conductivity screening of 1,432 s/cm was observed (Photos 13-14).-Remediation efforts were in progress at the time of inspection. Operators were observed scraping off impacted aggregates with heavy machinery (Photos 15-17).-A roll-off box arrived on site during the inspection. It was stated that the impacted material would be placed in the roll-off box and that waste manifests would be provided to the Department (Photo 18).Determination:Violations issued.

Comments: This is a producing combination well with a gas powered pumpjack attached. The well is plumbed to a 210 barrel stock tank and 50 barrel poly tank on site. It appears as though there has been a leak on this site recently. There is an area approximately 10x20 feet with staining of soil and dead vegetation, along with a finger of oil stained soil in an erosion rill about 20 feet further. The estimated volume released is unknown but appears to be less than a barrel. The operator was contacted regarding this issue and potential cleanup. At the time of the call, they said that another operator was contracted to pump this well at this time. However, they were mobilizing equipment for light excavation of the contaminated soil as soon as possible and would be following up on site shortly, and providing more information on the leak when it was available.In a return phone call, the operator stated that the contracting pumper noticed that the well was on paraffin for a significant amount of time. The operator brought in a treatment system that removed the paraffin from the well. Some was put into the drums on site or otherwise leaked and was not cleaned up. By the end of the day on 8/23, the operator had the site cleaned up and seeded and mulched. No further inspection of this site will be necessary at this time.

Comments: On October 30th, 2025, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of K Petroleum Inc's Mclvaine well site located in Somerset Township, Washington County following a voicemail and phone conversation where Operator Robert Inghram notified the Department of a 7-10 gallon release of crude oil from the production tank on to the ground within the tanks earthen dike. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the wellhead and a well posting fixed to the meter box on site, both of which had all required information posted on it. No active surface fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the wellhead, meter box, separator or fenced in production equipment on site.Upon inspection of the production tank, the Department observed a black tank to be within an earthen dike. The tank was observed to have orange/tan smudges and dried drip marks going down the side of it. What the Department believes may be peatsorb was observed on the ground at the base of the tank on top of puddles of fluid. This fluid had a possibly petroleum based odor and was observed to have an orange/tan film on top of it in some areas.The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the dike and collected soil conductivity readings of 0.826 mS and 0.904 mS in the release area, and 0.582 mS in berm of the dike. The Department also collected soil conductivity readings of 0.1705 mS and 0.1746 mS outside of where the peatsorb was observed. All of these readings were then compared to a background soil conductvitiy reading of 0.242 mS. The readings collected outside of the peatsorb are comparable to the background reading, subjugating that the release may be contained to the areas where peatsorb is observed. The readings within the fluid and in the side of the berm are elevated when compared to the background reading subjugating that the release has yet to be fully cleaned up.The Department recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with the Department's policy for small spills. The Operator is also requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.While on site, the Department spoke with Operator Robert Inghram and informed him of the Department's findings and of the aforementioned recommendations and requests. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for a 7-10 gallon release on to the ground from the production tank.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/26/2023 to ARMAC RESOURCES LLC in Warren City, Warren county. 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARMAC RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/26/2023
Violation Code: 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 8160049
Permit API: 123-45286
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Warren City
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 9/26/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an active stray gas migration case (CTS# 369563). Previously this well was found to have methane detected outside of the well bore and the operator decided to plug the well. Upon completion of their plugging attempt they inadvertently cemented some of their tubing into the well. Subsequently a camera was ran into the well and bubbles were visibly seen at the top of fluid level. A MSA Altair 5X gas meter was used and determined the bubbles were methane being emitted into the well bore. A violation was issued to the operator for not properly plugging the well. To address this violation the operator had a rig attempt to drill down to approx 550', which is 50' below the surface casing shoe and remove the cemented in tubing at which point another camera run would have taken place to see if the well is still bubbling methane. The rig failed to drill down to 550' and it was decided to cement the remaining tubing into the well. Top of cement is now at 288.23' with approx. 102' of tubing encapsulated within the well bore. ARMAC has now contracted Hornburg drilling to attempt to drill and clean out the well-bore to a depth of 550'. At the time of inspection Hornburg Drilling Rig 78 has drilled with a 4-1/2" work string and a 6-1/8" bit to a total depth of approx. 550'. A recording camera run was observed by myself and an ARMAC representative, and it revealed bubbling at fluid level (~550'). I placed a MSA ALTAIR 5X meter (calibrated 09-07-2023) into the well bore and got a non detect for methane, however due to the fact the well is still bubbling the department believes the well is not properly plugged to stop the vertical flow of methane within the well bore and the violation will continue.

Comments: On 07/24/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Southwestern's (SWN's) Vanorder-Patrick (12 Pad) Well Pad in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 70 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last24 hours. I arrived at 1035 hours. The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There are two post-construction stormwater management structures onsite. They appear to be functioning properly. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 192.8-262 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine gas processing units (GPUs) held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine wells capable of producing. There were each properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. There were numerous temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. Site remediation has been performed and a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEPs Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed.The DEP recommends:1. Disposing of stormwater held in the secondary containment structures as soon as possible to maintain compliance with 25 PA 78a64a(e).I departed at 1135 hours.
